about: Generated by tools/gen-map.py from the code. Do not edit by hand: run `make map`.

modules.description: Theme customisation, live.

Updates, from GitHub: every few hours (and shortly after login) the latest commit on main is compared with the one this machine was installed from. A newer one gives a notification, "GNOMAC: new update available", with Update / Later / What's new. In "auto" mode it is installed in the background and you are told to log in again. "off" does nothing.

Liquid Glass debug overlay, off by default (setting glass-debug, or Spotlight "Liquid Glass debug"). Shows the number of live glass surfaces, the quality level, the wallpaper brightness steering the glass, whether animations are on, and the frame rate. `glass-debug-mode` additionally shows one layer of the material alone (1 backdrop, 2 refraction, 3 fresnel, 4 specular, 5 rim, 6 tint) on every surface.
Start-up and shut-down animations, after macOS 26/27.

macOS 27 lock screen on top of GNOME's UnlockDialog (authentication, PAM, notifications and user switching stay GNOME's): - date and a very large clock at the top, never flying away, - avatar, name and a glass password pill at the bottom, - the wallpaper is crisp at rest and frosts while the prompt is up, - prompt rises with a fade instead of GNOME's zoom crossfade.
GDM login screen, in the macOS 27 style. Runs only in GDM's own shell (session mode "gdm"), where this extension is loaded once it has been installed system-wide (see gdm/install-gdm.sh).

Launchpad: full-screen app grid over frosted glass, opened from the dock's Applications button (or Super+A when enabled). Paged grid with dots, spring paging (scroll, arrows, swipe-like wheel), type-to-search, and the macOS zoom-in/zoom-out when it opens and closes.

macOS-style menu bar on top of the stock GNOME panel: system menu on the left, bold focused-app name with its menu, clock moved to the far right in the macOS format, Activities hidden. Golden Gate's menu bar is transparent by default; a Liquid Glass background is optional.

macOS menu bar menus for the focused app: File, Edit, View, (app extras such as Spotify's Playback), Window, Help. Like RevoShell's TopBar, the menus are described here rather than read from the app (GTK 4 apps no longer export menus); items send the app's real keyboard shortcut or act on its window through mutter, and show the shortcut macOS-style.

A menu bar on every screen but the primary one, as on macOS: the focused app's name on the left, the clock on the right. GNOME's own panel only exists on the primary monitor, so without this the other screens have none.

macOS-style dock: floating Liquid Glass pane, gaussian magnification that pushes neighbours apart (like the real dock, unlike a plain scale), launch bounce, running dots, tooltips and the stock GNOME app context menu.

Breathing room around maximized windows, like RevoShell's Hyprland gaps: thin invisible struts on the left, right and top edges keep maximized windows off the screen sides and away from the menu bar (the dock already reserves the bottom, plus the same gap above it).

Spotlight (Super+Space): a floating Liquid Glass search bar above the windows. Results: applications, a calculator, system actions and a web search fallback. Keyboard first: type, arrows to move, Enter to open, Escape to dismiss. Opening uses a spring so the bar "lands" like macOS.

Displays (Super + Ctrl + D): a small panel to manage several displays — which one is the main display, on which side of it each other one sits (left, right, above, below), turn one off or on, mirror, extend, or keep only one.
Liquid Glass for every shell menu: quick settings (restyled as a macOS Control Center), the calendar, app menus, dock menus, the system menu.

macOS window animations: open from the dock icon, close, minimize and restore into the dock icon (a curved path, or the Genie effect), maximise. The motion itself lives in lib/windowMotion.js (WindowMotionManager); this module is the bridge to GNOME's window manager signals.

Dynamic Island, modelled on RevoShell's: not a floating pill but a notch hanging from the top edge of the screen, flat against it, with concave "ears" blending into the edge and rounded bottom corners. - resting: artwork + equalizer on the left, the time in the middle, an unread-notification badge on the right (always visible), - hover / click with a player: grows into a media card (title, artist, app icon, progress bar, transport controls), - hover without a player: widens to show the full date, - workspace switch: the time briefly becomes workspace dots, - notification (optional setting): grows into a notification card. Width and height ride springs; the shape is redrawn with Cairo.

macOS notification banners: top-right corner, rounded Liquid Glass card that slides in under the menu bar. GNOME's banner logic (actions, reply, expansion, queueing) is untouched; only placement and material change.
Notification Center: every notification GNOME is holding, in one glass panel that slides in from the right edge (macOS style).

macOS "vibrancy" behind app sidebars: a frosted copy of the wallpaper is placed inside the window actor, under the app's own surface. Apps whose GTK theme leaves the sidebar translucent (GNOMAC's gtk.css does it for Files) then show glass there, while opaque areas hide it completely.
Desktop widgets (macOS 27): glass tiles on the wallpaper, under every window, that the user can add, remove, move, resize, colour and restyle.

Icons on the desktop: the files and folders of your Desktop folder, shown on the wallpaper and usable like on Windows / macOS: - click selects (Ctrl+click adds, drag on an empty spot draws a selection rectangle), double-click opens, - drag an icon (or several) to move it; it snaps to a grid and is remembered; drop it on the notch to keep it on the shelf, - keys: Enter open, F2 rename, Delete trash, Ctrl+A / C / X / V, - right-click an icon: Open, Rename, Copy, Cut, Copy Path, Keep on the Shelf, Move to Trash, - right-click the desktop: New Folder, New Text Document, Paste, Sort by, Refresh, Select All, Show Desktop Items, Open in Terminal, Change Background, Display Settings, - the folder is watched: files added, renamed or deleted elsewhere appear at once.

Wallpaper picker (RevoShell's coverflow): Super+W opens a dark full-screen carousel of wallpapers fanned out in 3D; arrows or the wheel move it on a spring, Enter applies. The new wallpaper is revealed by a circle growing from the centre of the screen, then handed to GNOME's settings.

macOS 27 status items on the right of the menu bar: Wi-Fi fan (or the Ethernet "<···>" glyph), a horizontal battery with its percentage, and the Control Center symbol. They live inside GNOME's quick settings button, so a click still opens the (glass) Control Center.

"Appearance" section of the Control Center, as in the macOS 27 Appearance settings: accent colour, light/dark/auto, Liquid Glass clear/tinted and the icon & widget style, all one click away from the menu bar.
Window tiling, as in macOS Sequoia/Golden Gate: halves, quarters, thirds, fill and centre.

Stage Manager, as a simplified version of macOS's: the window you work in stays on stage, every other window of the workspace steps aside into a strip of cards on the left. Click a card to bring that window on stage; the one it replaces goes to the strip.

lib.description: "About This Mac", after macOS 26/27: a glass card with a drawn machine, its model and name, three tabs (Overview, Displays, Storage) and the buttons More Info… (GNOME's own About page: a different place from System Settings), Software Update… and Report a Bug…

Adaptive glass: the wallpaper's brightness steers the material. Over a dark wallpaper the glass stays light and faint; over a bright one it darkens a touch, its edge becomes more visible and the highlight calmer, so panels and text stay readable. The change is continuous (no switch between two looks): everything follows `amount`, a smooth 0..1 "how bright is it".
AnimationTimeline: every time-based animation of the desktop motion system runs on the ONE metronome of the extension (lib/spring.js getTicker()), not on a timer or Clutter.Timeline of its own.

Timers for the benchmarks (Spotlight: "Glass Benchmark", "Motion Benchmark") that can all be stopped at once. A benchmark runs for tens of seconds, and the module that started it can be switched off in the middle: its timers must not keep repainting and moving windows after that.

The drawings of the start-up animation, as in macOS 26/27 "Hello": - the logo is traced with a line, then fills with glass and a sheen sweeps across it, - greeting words are written stroke by stroke in a script, in glass.
Tiny arithmetic evaluator for Spotlight. Never uses eval(): a recursive descent parser over + - * / % ^ and parentheses, accepting × ÷ and a decimal comma so "12,5 × 4" works with a French keyboard.

Clipboard history shared by Spotlight (Clipboard mode) and the Dynamic Island. It only exists while at least one module uses it, and is wiped when the last one stops: copied passwords never outlive the session UI. The data and its rules live in clipboardStore.js (tested apart).

The clipboard history as plain data, with no link to the shell: it is shared by Spotlight and the Dynamic Island (lib/clipboardHistory.js feeds it), and it only exists while at least one of them uses it.
Album covers for the Dynamic Island.

The desktop layer: one transparent, full-screen layer that desktop icons and widgets live on, and that takes the desktop's own clicks (so the right-click menu is ours, and the same with or without a wallpaper window).

GNOMAC Diagnostics (Spotlight > "GNOMAC Diagnostics"): what this machine and this shell really are, in one panel, also saved to ~/.cache/gnomac/diagnostics.txt so it can be pasted in a bug report. A value that cannot be read is shown as N/A. Nothing is guessed.

What the screen really is: resolution and refresh rate of each monitor, read from Mutter's DisplayConfig service (the same source as GNOME Settings). Nothing is assumed: until the answer arrives, or if it cannot be read, `refreshHz` is null ("N/A"), never 60.

Multi-monitor layouts: from what Mutter's DisplayConfig service reports to what it is asked to apply. Only arithmetic lives here (nothing touches the shell), so it can be tested on its own (tools/test-display-layout.mjs).

Choose files from inside the shell, through the desktop portal (org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser), the same dialog every app uses. The shell cannot open a GTK dialog itself; the portal can, and needs nothing installed beyond xdg-desktop-portal-gnome (part of GNOME).

Install (or check) GNOMAC's login screen from inside the desktop: Spotlight > "Install the Login Screen". The part that needs administrator rights runs through pkexec: the system's own password dialog appears; GNOMAC never sees, asks for or stores the password.

macOS Genie: the window is sucked into its dock icon through a narrowing funnel. Same model as RevoShell's Genie.qml: the window snapshot is cut into horizontal strips; rows nearest the dock leave first (smootherstep timing) and each strip is moved and squeezed towards the icon.
Liquid Glass material.

Glass benchmark: N surfaces (1, 5, 10, 20, 50), once as separate GlassSurface and once as GlassContainer groups of 8 regions, repainted on every frame for 3 s each. Run it from Spotlight ("Glass Benchmark"); the results go to ~/.cache/gnomac/glass-bench.json and a notification.
GlassContainer: several glass regions drawn as ONE piece of glass.
GlassPerformanceManager: watches the frame rate while the desktop is animating and lowers (then, carefully, raises) the quality of the glass.
Liquid Glass design tokens: every number that shapes the material or its motion lives here (docs/liquid-glass.md). Components never carry their own.
"Guide GNOMAC": a glass sheet with every shortcut and gesture of the project, found by typing "guide" in Spotlight. Same content as the README.

Greeting words as vector paths (1000-unit em, y down, baseline at 0), made from the Sacramento font by Astigmatic, SIL Open Font License 1.1 (https://scripts.sil.org/OFL). Generated by tools/make_hello.py: do not edit.
Minimal two-language strings until proper gettext catalogs exist.
Sends keyboard shortcuts to the focused window, so menu bar items like Edit › Copy act on the app the way the real shortcut would.
The start-up lens: a disc of liquid glass that opens at the centre of the screen and grows until it covers it (modules/bootShutdown.js, style "lens").

GNOME Shell keeps, for each popup menu, the "settings" items added with addSettingsAction() (Network, Bluetooth, power profiles... in the quick settings) and sets their visibility at every change of session mode, i.e. at every lock and unlock. When such an item is destroyed (a network device or a Bluetooth device goes away), GNOME forgets to drop it from that list: the next lock then writes to a destroyed object, and the journal fills with a warning and a stack trace for each one (hundreds over a few days, each costing time at the very moment the screen locks or unlocks).

MissionControl: the windows of the current workspace shrink and arrange themselves on a grid; a click on one brings it back to full size and focuses it. The REAL window actors are transformed (translation + scale): nothing is destroyed or recreated, no clones.
Apple-style micro-interactions shared by the island, widgets and menus.
Motion benchmark (Spotlight > "Motion Benchmark"): runs the real window animations on YOUR open windows and measures what the screen actually does.

Motion tokens: one set of durations and curves for the whole desktop, so a window, the dock, Spotlight, the island and a workspace change feel like one physical system. Everything is ease-out or critically damped: no bounce, no overshoot (the only exception, the dock's notification badge, is documented).
A small MPRIS client, straight over D-Bus, for the Dynamic Island.
More Dynamic Island pages: system stats, quick actions, clipboard, and the "idle home" shown in place of the player when nothing is playing.

Extra views of the Dynamic Island, as in Alcove / Boring Notch: - MonthCalendar: the current month with today highlighted, - PomodoroTimer: focus/break countdown shown as an orange ring when the notch is folded, - Shelf: files kept in the notch, one click opens them.
Clicking a notification must open what it is about.

The "Prayers" tab of the Dynamic Island: the next prayer and how long until it, the six times of the day with the current one lit, and the date in the Hijri calendar. Everything is computed on the machine (lib/prayerTimes.js).
The "Heures de prière" group of the preferences window. It lives apart from prefs.js because it is long, and because it runs in the preferences process (GTK, no shell): it imports no shell module.

The prayer times of a day as real moments (GLib.DateTime), which prayer is current and which is next, and the alerts that fire at each prayer. The astronomy lives in prayerTimes.js; this file only deals with clocks.

Prayer times, computed on the machine from the sun's position: no network, no account. The formulas are the usual astronomical ones (solar declination and equation of time, then the hour at which the sun reaches a given angle below or above the horizon). Nothing here touches the shell: it only turns a date and a place into times, so it can be tested on its own.
The desktop is REVEALED in two beats, shared by the unlock transition and the start-up:
Session actions for the system menu and Spotlight.
GLSLEffect: the base class of every GNOMAC shader.
Spring physics shared by every GNOMAC animation.

A small SVG path reader for Cairo: absolute and relative M L H V C S Q T Z, curves flattened only to measure lengths. A parsed path is a list of subpaths (the contours), each with its own length and horizontal extent, so a drawing animation can trace every contour by its own dash progress.

Lets an event handler run at most once per interval. A mouse sends motion events at 125 Hz to 1000 Hz; the screen shows at most one picture per frame, so work done for every event beyond that is wasted.

Shared sizing helper. Every pixel size in GNOMAC was designed on a 1280x800 logical screen; on a taller logical screen (a bigger VM window, a 4K monitor at scale 1) fixed pixels look tiny. The factor follows the primary monitor's logical height, so HiDPI scaling (which already shrinks the logical size) is handled too.

Weather for the desktop widget, from wttr.in (JSON, no API key). With no city configured the service locates the request by IP address, so the widget can be turned off or pinned to a city in the preferences.

"What's new": a glass card listing the new features and the fixes of the releases you have not seen yet. Shown once after an update (the first session that runs the new version), and from Spotlight > "What's new in GNOMAC". The notes are whatsnew.json, shipped with the extension.

More desktop widgets: analog clock, world clocks, day/week/month/year progress, countdown, photo, live CPU/memory graph and a weather forecast. Same contract as lib/widgetTypes.js: build(ctx) -> {actor, destroy?, update?, tick?, flush?}. ctx.accent is an [r, g, b] colour (0..1) or null.

Desktop widget types. Every type is {id, title, icon, sizes, build(ctx)}: build() receives a context and returns {actor, destroy, update?}. The layout manager (modules/widgets.js) owns glass, placement, editing and persistence; a type only fills its tile's content.
WindowMotionManager: the one place that moves windows.

tools.description: Check the GObject Introspection names used by the extension against the typelibs installed on this machine.
Static checks, the same ones the CI runs.
Sort the CRITICAL / JS ERROR lines of a GNOME Shell log into BENIGN SHUTDOWN and REAL BUG.
Builds the map of GNOMAC from the code itself: docs/MAP.md (for people) and docs/map.json (for programs and AI agents).
Turn greeting words into SVG path data using the OFL font Sacramento, so the extension can draw them (no font needs to be installed).
Render plymouth/gnomac/logo.png from icons/apple.svg's path: glass-white body with a soft vertical shading and a fading reflection underneath (same look as the start-up animation).
Builds the prayer part of the preferences in a small window of its own and drives it, so a typing mistake or a broken search shows up in a test.
Helpers for writing your own scenario for the headless GNOME Shell of tools/smoke-test.sh: wait, log, screenshots, a virtual keyboard and pointer, a real window, and a look at the modal grab that…
Test driver for tools/smoke-test.sh. It is copied into a throw-away copy of the extension and run inside a headless GNOME Shell: it opens and closes every panel that has an open/close pair, turns…
Start GNOME Shell headless with the extension from this checkout, in a throw-away session (own D-Bus, own settings, own data dir), drive it with tools/smoke-driver.js and report what GNOMAC logs.
The size cap on album covers (lib/coverArt.js): web addresses are capped while the data arrives, `data:` addresses before they are decoded.
lib/displayLayout.js: what is asked of Mutter for each multi-monitor action.
Runs install.sh --update and uninstall.sh in a throw-away home (own D-Bus, in-memory settings), and the login screen sync script as an ordinary user, to check that: - a gnomac.css of your own…
The transport buttons of the island (lib/mprisClient.js skipControl).
Pure logic of the island that has no need of the shell: the transport buttons and the clipboard history.
Checks lib/prayerSchedule.js: which prayer is current and next, the wall clock around a daylight-saving change, and the alerts.
Checks lib/prayerTimes.js against reference timetables from the Aladhan API (api.aladhan.com, fetched for the dates below).
lib/throttle.js: at most one pass per interval, and enter/leave never dropped.
The "Weather widget" setting must stop every request to wttr.in.
Trace a black-on-light logo bitmap into smooth SVG Bezier paths.

installAndSystem.description: GNOMAC installer — CachyOS / Arch first, works on any GNOME 50+ distro.
Removes GNOMAC and gives GNOME the look it had before ./install.sh: - the extension and its settings, - the GTK window controls, - the window buttons, fonts, icon/cursor theme, colour scheme, accent…
GNOMAC, express install: one command, a few questions, everything set up.
Remembers the GNOME settings GNOMAC changes, so uninstall.sh can put them back.
GNOMAC updater: fetch the newest version and refresh the extension and styles.
GNOMAC on the GDM login screen (CachyOS / Arch GNOME).
Copies the user's GNOMAC extension to the system folder GDM reads, so the login screen follows updates.
The two systemd units of the login screen auto-sync, as functions that print them.
GNOMAC login screen: your own CSS.
GNOMAC login screen settings (read by GDM's shell at each boot).
GNOME Shell's own typelibs are not on the runner: the library-name check runs on a machine with GNOME (tools/check.sh locally).
